assignments.rationale: X and Y both give highly structured, lettered (A/B/C/D) breakdowns with many named studies and granular protocol numbers; X is marginally the most exhaustive (adds SPME + TOP-assay + filtration subsections). Z is comparably informative but shorter and less structurally elaborated, suggesting a narrower retrieval set.

Z is by far the most comprehensive, citing five distinct method types with chain-specific numeric LOD/LOQ values and reconciling conflicting patterns. X gives a moderate set of examples; Y is the thinnest, resting on a single review with only one implied chain-length relationship.

X uniquely spans multiple technology classes (electrochemical, plasma, ultrasonication) with bullet synthesis, suggesting broader retrieval. Y and Z overlap heavily on electrochemical pH/electrolyte mechanisms; Y includes slightly more quantitative rate-enhancement figures than Z.

Z provides the most granular, analyte-resolved EE/O values (PFBA/PFHxA/PFOA/PFDA) and a defluorination-based energy metric, indicating the richest retrieval. X is broad but less analyte-specific; Y leans more qualitative/LCA-oriented with fewer precise figures.

Z uniquely names the source study (Cantoni et al.) and specific particle-size details (20-50 vs 90-125 um), showing the most precise retrieval. Y is moderately detailed; X is shortest and most hedged, admitting almost no comparable data was found.

X ends with the clearest two-part categorized summary and repeats precise quoted phrases, suggesting strongest synthesis. Y adds a unique term (membrane capacitive deionization) suggesting keyword-driven hybrid retrieval. Z is comparatively shorter and less structured.

Y includes the most concrete numeric anchor (99.999% destruction vs 62.6% defluorination) integrated cleanly into the endpoint framework. X is well-organized but less numeric. Z self-rates lower confidence (partially_answerable) and admits lacking a unified framework.

Z uniquely names a source (Steigerwald et al.) and enumerates five regeneration categories plus agricultural-matrix specifics, indicating the deepest retrieval. X and Y are similar in breadth but stay generic without named studies; Y is marginally thinner.

Y uniquely pulls in a second, comparative PAC/GAC source alongside the core kinetics study, indicating broader retrieval. Z contains the most precise quoted figure ('360 min to reach 90%'). X relies on a single source with straightforward numbers only.

Z integrates the widest range of evidence (mechanism, gas-phase analytical gaps, and field-validation numbers), suggesting richest retrieval. Y covers mechanism and byproducts but less breadth. X relies on a single study and is the shortest.

Y has the densest quantitative detail (Freundlich KF trends, r2=0.97, sludge removal percentages, PEI-modified nanofiber data), suggesting strongest retrieval. Z uniquely adds a nanofiltration/membrane angle. X is comparatively general and shorter.

Y uniquely surfaces a nuanced counterexample (an electrochemical anode where headgroup did not control performance), suggesting deeper synthesis across sources. X provides precise quantitative percentage comparisons. Z is detailed but comparatively narrower in synthesis.

Y explicitly names three separate studies (Kempisty et al., Park et al., Belkouteb et al.), indicating the most precise, wide-ranging retrieval. X is similarly reasoned but less explicitly attributed. Z covers similar ground but without named authors and flags conflicting evidence.
